events.title: European Markets Fail To Hold Early Gains, Settle Weak
events.description:
After trading in positive territory for much of the day's trading session, most of the markets in Europe ended weak on Tuesday, hurt by some brisk selling in the final hour. 

Despite oil's retreat, investors turned cautious amid continued uncertainty about Iran and the U.S. reaching an agreement to end their conflict anytime soon.

events.title: U.S. Job Openings Fall More Than Expected In August
events.description: The Labor Department released a report on Tuesday showing job openings in the U.S decreased by more than expected in the month of August.

events.title: U.S. Consumer Confidence Index Unexpectedly Slumps In September
events.description: A report released by the Conference Board on Tuesday unexpectedly showed a notable deterioration in U.S. consumer confidence in the month of September. The Conference Board said its consumer confidence index slumped to 81.9 in September from a downwardly revised 88.6 in August.

events.title: Bay Street Likely To Open With Positive Bias
events.description:
Canadian stocks may open with a positive bias on Tuesday as oil shed early gains and slipped into negative territory, and gold prices edged higher.

According to a flash estimate, the Canadian GDP is expected to have expanded by 0.2% from the previous month in August.

events.title: Eurozone Economic Sentiment Weakens
events.description: Eurozone economic confidence weakened unexpectedly in September due to the fall in consumer sentiment, monthly survey data from the European Commission showed Tuesday. The economic sentiment index dropped to 97.9 in September from 98.4 in the previous month. The score was forecast to rise to 99.0.

events.title: Major European Markets Move Higher As Oil Pares Early Gains
events.description: The major European markets gained some ground in positive territory on Tuesday with investors picking up select stocks even as oil prices remained at elevated levels despite coming off early highs and bond yields continued to hover around multi-year highs.

events.title: UK Mortgage Approvals Fall To 32-Month Low
events.description: UK mortgage approvals declined to a 32-month low in August amid higher borrowing costs, while consumer credit reached a record high, data from the Bank of England showed Tuesday. Net mortgage approvals for house purchases, an indicator of future borrowing, fell unexpectedly to 54,918 in August from 55,928 in the previous month.

events.title: Mixed Sentiment In Asian Markets
events.description: Mixed sentiment prevailed in Asian markets on Tuesday tracking the negative sentiment in Wall Street on Monday. Market mood was impacted by worries about a broad slowdown in AI development. Markets also digested the rate hike by Reserve Bank of Australia. Renewed diplomatic push to end the Middle East crisis, the decline in crude oil prices and the easing in bond yields capped losses.

events.title: Sensex, Nifty Come Off Early Lows, But Close Weak For 2nd Straight Session
events.description: Indian shares closed weak on Tuesday, extending recent losses, amid concerns about inflation due to elevated oil prices. Sustained selling by foreign portfolio investors weighed as well on stocks.

events.title: FTSE 100 Modestly Higher As Miners, Pharma Stocks Move Up
events.description: The U.K. stock market's benchmark index FTSE 100 climbed higher on Tuesday, led by gains in mining and pharmaceuticals sectors even as the mood remained somewhat cautious amid a lack of progress in U.S.-Iran negotiations to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

events.title: U.S. Dollar Rises Amid Fed Rate Hike Speculation
events.description: The U.S. dollar strengthened against most major currencies in the European session on Tuesday, as traders anticipate that the Federal Reserve (Fed) will raise interest rates twice more this year.

events.title: CAC 40 Up Marginally; Legrand Rises Over 7%
events.description: Despite higher oil prices and bond yields, France's equity benchmark CAC 40 edged marginally higher Tuesday morning thanks to strong buying at select counters, including Legrand and STMicroelectronics.

events.title: U.S. Dollar Rises Against Most Majors
events.description: The U.S. dollar strengthened against other major currencies in the European session on Tuesday.
